requirement: Issue a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token, refuse to accept either where the other is required, and exchange a refresh token for a fresh access token.
skeleton: WrongTokenTypeError, TTL constants, a private _encode helper, issue_pair validating the subject, read_token requiring and checking typ, and refresh_access built on read_token.
caption: Access and refresh JWTs kept apart with PyJWT and HS256. WrongTokenTypeError subclasses jwt.InvalidTokenError. A private _encode helper takes one UTC now and signs sub, typ, iat and exp = now plus a TTL, where ACCESS_TTL is 15 minutes and REFRESH_TTL is 7 days. issue_pair(secret, subject) raises ValueError saying the subject must not be empty and otherwise returns an access token and a refresh token. read_token(secret, token, expected_typ) decodes with algorithms pinned to HS256 and options requiring sub, typ and exp, so a token without typ raises jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError and a wrong secret raises jwt.InvalidSignatureError; a typ other than the expected one raises WrongTokenTypeError. refresh_access(secret, refresh_token) reads the token as a refresh token and mints a new access token for the same subject. The fixture asserts that the pair decodes with typ access and a 900 second lifetime and typ refresh and a 604800 second lifetime, that each token is rejected where the other type is expected, that refreshing yields an access token for alice lasting 900 seconds, that an access token cannot refresh, that a token without typ raises jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError, that another secret raises jwt.InvalidSignatureError, and that an empty subject raises ValueError.

constraints: Access tokens live 15 minutes and refresh tokens 7 days
Each token carries a typ claim of access or refresh
A token of the wrong type raises WrongTokenTypeError
A missing typ claim raises jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError
Only refresh tokens can be exchanged, and the exchange yields an access token

rationale.teaches: Stamp a typ claim on every token, require it at decode time, and compare it against the type the caller expects before trusting the claims.
rationale.why: Both token kinds are signed with the same secret, so without a typ check a stolen week-long refresh token works as an access token everywhere.

ops.docstring: Keep access and refresh JWTs apart with a typ claim and separate lifetimes.

ops.source:
class WrongTokenTypeError(jwt.InvalidTokenError):
    """A token of one type was presented where the other type was required."""

def issue_pair(secret: str, subject: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token."""
    if not subject:
        raise ValueError("subject must not be empty")
    access = _encode(secret, subject, "access", ACCESS_TTL)
    refresh = _encode(secret, subject, "refresh", REFRESH_TTL)
    return access, refresh

def read_token(secret: str, token: str, expected_typ: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Verify the token and insist that its typ claim is the expected one."""
    claims: dict[str, Any] = jwt.decode(
        token,
        secret,
        algorithms=[ALGORITHM],
        options={"require": ["sub", "typ", "exp"]},
    )
    if claims["typ"] != expected_typ:
        raise WrongTokenTypeError(f"expected a {expected_typ} token")
    return claims

candidates.why_wrong: The typ claim is never compared, so refresh tokens pass as access tokens.
Refresh tokens last seven hours instead of seven days.
The exchange demands an access token, so real refresh tokens are refused and access tokens renew themselves.
typ is not required, so a token without it crashes with KeyError instead of a JWT error.
The exchange mints another refresh token, which cannot be used as an access token.
